summary_points: Document title: TES S&T HEX Functional Description of Standby and Drainage Procedures
Client: Arizona Solar One, Project: HEX replacement TES Solana
Document number: 4521-MEM-AEE-70-10-0001-GAR, Revision: 01
Purpose: IFD (Instruction For Development)
Prepared by Manuel Muñoz Arranz and Ricardo Rodolfo Delgado Amaya, Reviewed and Approved by José Maria Rodriguez León
Document contains sections on HEX Trains, Instrumentation, Molten Salt Drainage System, Logic Control, Standby Sequence, and HEX Drainage Operation
Document describes standby and drainage procedures for Shell and Tube HEX in TES System
CCR divided into SF-HTF, SG-STG, and TES operating stations
Procedure based on semi-automatic/manual operation
TES HEX transfers energy between HTF and molten salt
Six TES trains with six shell and tube heat exchangers each
Drainage system evacuates molten salt using gravity and additional N2
Main components include drain back tank (XX-MT-257) and pump (XX-MP-258)
Tags 'XX' in tank and pump TAGs are replaced with numbers 1, 2, or 3
The TES HEX drainage and vent system uses manual and automated controls.
Drain back pump operates based on specific signals with interlocks and alarms.
On/Off control valves are manually operated with associated DCS signals.
Control loops maintain the level of molten salt drain back tank using PID controllers.
Interlocks prevent mixing of molten salt from different TES trains.
Transition to standby from charge mode involves reducing HTF flow and adjusting salt flow.
Standby sequence includes shutting down TES units and adjusting main salt pump speed.
HEX drainage operation requires opening manual valves and starting the drain back tank pump.
